# dsh-session-fulltext-search
Enable full-text search over DSH session history in the Web sidebar — and make it actually find Chin
xt search over DSH session history in the Web sidebar — and make it actually find Chinese text. 中文说明

The DeepSeek Harness web UI ships with a content-search backend
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query-sql

ite`, SQLite FTS5) that is **disabled by
default** (`openAt: never`): the sidebar magnifier then mat

ches only session
titles and workspace names. This plugin is the deployment override the
backend's d

ocumentation prescribes — `openAt: first-search` with a persistent
derived index under `$DSH_HOME`.

That alone has a catch for CJK users: FTS5's `unicode61` tokenizer treats a
run of continuous Chines

e text as **one token**, so a query only matches when
it aligns with token boundaries — searching `福

州大学` does not hit
`已保研至福州大学`. This plugin therefore also mounts a **substring fallback**:
queries co

ntaining CJK are answered with a literal substring scan over the
same derived index, so any Chinese

phrase inside message bodies is found,
exactly as you typed it. Non-CJK queries use the tokenizer un

nside message bodies is found,
exactly as you typed it. Non-CJK queries use the tokenizer unchanged.
## What you get

- The sidebar magnifier searches **message bodies** (user messages, assistant
replies) across all wo

rkspaces, with a content snippet per hit.
- **Chinese searches are substring-based** — no whole-toke

n boundary problem.
- The index updates incrementally as sessions grow.
## Install
Into a profile (e.g. `desktop`):

`dsh plugin add` also registers the package in `dsh.profile.bundles` (the
patch-layer stack). Restar
t DSH afterwards. Manual equivalent:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
then `pnpm install` inside the profile directory and restart DSH.
## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]

After restarting DSH the sidebar falls back to title-only search. The derived
index file (`$DSH_HOME
/session-query-index.sqlite3`) can be deleted.
## Notes

- CJK queries take the substring scan; other queries keep the tokenizer's
word/phrase matching (so `

pytho` still does not match `python` — by design,
that is how FTS5 works). Wrap a query in quotes (`

"two words"`) for
exact-phrase search; FTS5 operators (`OR`, `*`) are treated as plain text.
- The f

allback reads the derived index with its own read-only SQLite
connection; the owning engine keeps wr

iting (WAL). A missing or rebuilding
index simply returns fewer results for that one query.
- This l

ayer only overrides the `session-query-sqlite` row's config
(`path`, `openAt`) and adds its own wrap

per row. Your own profile
`cordis.patch.yml` sits later in the stack, so a manual override there sti

ll
wins over this plugin.
- The index is derived data — delete the file to force a rebuild. Never po

int
`path` at the session persistence database.
